name: product-manager-os-routing
doc: Tiered model routing for the Product Manager OS. Contract, doctrine, and setup live in routing/README.md. Values in ${VAR} form are resolved from the environment by the caller; never commit resolved values.

requestHeaders.doc: Send on every call. Compression would paraphrase text the model must quote verbatim; the router's semantic cache would replay one bad temperature-0 answer to every similar prompt; memory and skill injection change the prompt the model sees. The response echoes X-OmniRoute-Compression, X-OmniRoute-Cache and X-OmniRoute-Model; log them with each artifact.

verify.doc: A tier name is not proof a model is connected. Probe each tier with a one-line prompt before a run; a 404 'Combo has no executable targets' means no connected provider serves that tier. See routing/README.md, 'Verify the tiers before trusting them'.
verify.expectedOnKeylessInstall: auto/cheap, auto/coding and auto/reasoning answer from the free model; auto/reasoning:pro returns 404 until a provider with a pro reasoning model is connected

extraction.purpose: Mechanical transforms where the answer is checkable: pull fields from documents, normalize backlogs, tag and summarize sources, convert formats, check a draft against a template's field list.

drafting.purpose: First complete drafts of structured artifacts: fill one named template from supplied evidence, write ADRs, produce diagrams-as-code, restructure a document without changing its claims.

judgment.purpose: Work where being wrong is expensive and unverifiable locally: prioritization calls, premortems, red-team passes, gap analyses, gate reviews, anything a human will sign.
judgment.requires: A connected provider that serves a pro reasoning model (a Claude Code, Codex or Gemini subscription via OAuth, or an API-key provider). On a keyless install this tier returns 404 'Combo has no executable targets' and judgment work queues; it is never routed to the cheap tier silently.

keylessFallback.doc: Opt-in only. When enabled, judgment work on an install with no pro provider runs on auto/reasoning (the free reasoning model) and every artifact produced must carry the line 'judgment tier: degraded, reviewed by a person before use'. Off by default because rule 3 in routing/README.md says queue, not downgrade.

fixedFallback.doc: Optional recipe for deployments that must pin exact models instead of auto tiers. Replace the placeholders with model IDs your OmniRoute instance serves, in preference order; the first available model in the list is used. Leave enabled false to stay on auto tiers.

limits.doc: Fail closed: at the cap, halt the tier and queue the work; never overspend and never silently downgrade judgment work to a cheaper tier.
